title: Efficacy of Tecovirimat for the Treatment of Mpox Virus Infection in Humans: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review evaluates the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for the treatment of mpox virus infection in humans, focusing on clinical outcomes such as time to clinical resolution of skin lesions, lesion resolution by day 28-29, and 28-day all-cause mortality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were conducted, searching PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to June 5, 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Tecovirimat did not significantly shorten the time to clinical resolution of skin lesions compared with placebo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.52-2.31, GRADE: moderate) or increase lesion resolution by day 28-29 (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.08, GRADE: high). Virological clearance, pain-related outcomes, and serious adverse events were also comparable between treatment groups.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No statistical heterogeneity was observed (I 2 = 0% for both outcomes). However, mortality at day 28 was rare in both trials, precluding meta-analysis. The review highlights the need for further evidence to determine whether selected high-risk populations may benefit from antiviral therapy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Current randomized evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use to accelerate clinical recovery or improve mortality rates in patients with mpox. Further research is needed to explore its potential benefits in specific high-risk populations.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the efficacy and safety of tecovirimat for treating mpox virus infection in humans. Two low-risk-of-bias RCTs involving 941 participants were analyzed, focusing on clinical outcomes such as time to skin lesion resolution and 28-day mortality. The results indicate that tecovirimat does not significantly improve clinical resolution or reduce mortality compared to placebo or standard care. Virological clearance and adverse events were comparable between groups. However, due to the rarity of mortality events, meta-analysis of this outcome was not possible. The review concludes that current evidence does not support routine tecovirimat use, but further research is needed to determine its potential benefits in high-risk populations.

title: Mpox and sexually transmitted infections: syndemic drivers of transmission and disease outcomes-A Narrative Review

analysis.scope_and_question: The worldwide outbreak of mpox (formerly monkeypox) in 2022 emerged as a public health emergency posing greater threat to persons with sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A narrative review was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar to identify relevant literature published between 2008 and 2026, focusing on mpox, STIs, co-infections, and pregnancy outcomes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Epidemiological data reveal that STIs such as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Chlamydia trachomatis, herpes simplex virus, syphilis have been frequently associated with mpox infection highlighting the role of sexual contact in its transmission.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: STI co-infection may be associated with mucosal invasion and immune modulation plausibly affecting disease progression, however direct mechanistic evidence remains limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Recognizing these factors is important for screening, early diagnosis and management strategies to mitigate future outbreaks and impact of mpox.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the syndemic interactions between mpox and sexually transmitted infections (STIs), emphasizing the role of sexual networks in transmission dynamics. The review highlights that STIs such as HIV, Chlamydia trachomatis, herpes simplex virus, and syphilis are frequently associated with mpox infection, suggesting that sexual contact is a significant mode of transmission. While the review acknowledges the potential biological, behavioral, and structural factors influencing mpox transmission and clinical outcomes, it notes that direct mechanistic evidence linking STIs to disease progression remains limited. The findings underscore the importance of integrating STI screening and management into mpox prevention and control strategies to address the unique risks posed by co-infections, particularly in vulnerable populations such as gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) and pregnant women.

title: Epidemiological and sociodemographic profile of Mpox in Brazilian Amazon: a cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the epidemiological and sociodemographic profile of Mpox in the Brazilian Amazon, as the outbreak showed viral transmission within sexual networks and atypical clinical presentations. The research aimed to characterize the demographic and clinical features of Mpox cases in this region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study used data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) between March 2022 and December 2025. The sample included 296 cases, divided into confirmed Mpox cases (G1; n = 86) and ruled-out cases (G2; n = 210).
analysis.methods: The study was observational and analytical, following STROBE guidelines. Associations were evaluated using statistical tests such as Pearson's Chi-square test and Fisher's exact test, with significance set at p < 0.05 in SPSS v.26.0.
analysis.main_results: In confirmed Mpox cases (G1), infection was concentrated among men (97.7%), adults aged 19 to 59 years (98.8%), residents of Belém (76.7%), individuals with tertiary education (53.5%), and those reporting homosexual (73.3%) or bisexual (12.8%) orientation. Fever (81.4%) and localized genital lesions (43.0% in G1 vs. 6.2% in G2) were the primary clinical presentations. Intimate sexual contact was the main exposure pathway (65.1%). A high proportion of HIV coinfection was observed in G1 (54.7%), with 23.3% presenting an active STI at notification, predominantly syphilis (16.3%). Clinical management was predominantly outpatient, with a 7.0% hospitalization rate and a 96.5% cure rate among valid confirmed cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Mpox cases in Pará were concentrated in the state capital and associated with intimate sexual contact networks among young adults. They noted the high coinfection frequencies with HIV and syphilis, highlighting a novel association between Mpox and these conditions in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted surveillance and prevention strategies in the Brazilian Amazon, particularly focusing on high-risk groups such as men who have sex with men and individuals with HIV. They also emphasize the need for integrated approaches to address co-occurring STIs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a cross-sectional design, which limits causal inference. The sample size is relatively small, and the data are sourced from a notification system, which may introduce reporting biases. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study analyzed Mpox cases in the Brazilian Amazon from 2022 to 2025, focusing on sociodemographic and clinical profiles. The study found that Mpox was concentrated among men, particularly those in Belém, aged 19 to 59, with tertiary education, and reporting homosexual or bisexual orientation. Fever and localized genital lesions were the primary clinical presentations, with intimate sexual contact as the main exposure pathway. A high proportion of HIV coinfection and active STIs, especially syphilis, was observed. Clinical management was mostly outpatient, with a high cure rate. The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the role of sexual networks and co-occurring STIs in Mpox transmission. The study's moderate evidence strength is due to its observational design and reliance on notification data, which may introduce biases.

title: Disclosing pathogenic processes of monkeypox (MPOX) and drug repurposing through host-transcriptomics analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Monkeypox (MPOX) virus infection outbreak in Africa in 2022 was initially considered a neglected tropical disease (NTD). Now it is recognized as a global health problem.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study attempted to disclose pathogenic processes and therapeutic strategies of MPOX based on MPOX-associated host key-genes (hKGs).
analysis.methods: At first, three transcriptomic profile datasets were analyzed, identifying 166 common host differentially expressed genes (hDEGs) between MPOX patients and control groups, comprising 75 upregulated and 91 downregulated hDEGs.
analysis.main_results: Functional enrichment analysis of these hKGs revealed critical pathogenic processes of MPOX infection, including biological processes, molecular functions, cellular components, and KEGG pathways. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the top three complexes (ALB-Tecovirimat, CDH1-Maraviroc, and PPARG-Beclabuvir) demonstrated strong binding stability, supported by RMSD, RMSF, and MM-GBSA results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Based on molecular docking analysis, five top-ranked drug molecules Tecovirimat, Beclabuvir, Maraviroc, Raltegravir, and Brincidofovir were identified as potential repurposable therapeutics against MPOX.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provided in this study might be potential resources for diagnosis and therapies of MPOX patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: However, the findings require experimental validation in wet lab for further confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to uncover the pathogenic mechanisms of the monkeypox virus and identify potential drug repurposing strategies. By analyzing transcriptomic profiles, the researchers identified 166 differentially expressed host genes, including six key genes involved in MPOX pathogenesis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested Tecovirimat, Beclabuvir, Maraviroc, Raltegravir, and Brincidofovir as promising therapeutic candidates. The findings highlight potential diagnostic and therapeutic resources for MPOX patients but emphasize the need for wet lab validation to confirm their efficacy. The study contributes to understanding the molecular basis of MPOX and offers new avenues for drug development, though its results are based on computational models and require further experimental testing.

analysis.methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were stimulated with inactivated MPV and then exposed to aminoadamantane (AMA) and its derivative, 3F2. The activation status of monocytes, NK, and NKT cells was assessed, along with the levels of immunosoluble mediators such as chemokines and cytokines.
analysis.main_results: MPV stimulation led to significant changes in immunosoluble mediator levels, including reductions in chemokines and cytokines crucial for antiviral defense and immune regulation. Treatment with 3F2 significantly increases levels of key mediators such as CCL2, CXCL8, IFN-γ, and growth factors like VEGF and NGF-β, indicating its potential as an immunomodulatory candidate. The findings suggest that 3F2 could be a promising therapeutic option for modulating immune responses in mpox disease. title: Conservation guided reverse vaccinology for the design of a broadly immunogenic multi-epitope vaccine against monkeypox virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox, caused by the Monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a global public health concern following outbreaks beyond its traditional endemic regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A dataset of 27 complete MPXV genomes (2001–2025) from diverse geographic regions was analyzed to identify highly conserved viral genes.
analysis.methods: Conserved surface-exposed proteins were prioritized for epitope prediction, including cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on binding affinity, antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and absence of human sequence homology. Promiscuous epitopes with broad human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding were curated to maximize population coverage.
analysis.main_results: Three multi-epitope vaccine constructs were designed using appropriate linkers and adjuvants. Structural modeling, molecular docking with innate immune receptors, immune response simulation, and codon optimization were performed to evaluate the constructs. All constructs were predicted to be stable, antigenic, and non-allergenic.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Vaccine construct 2 (VC2) was predicted to have the strongest interactions with TLR2 and the TLR4–MD-2 complex, achieving the highest binding affinities (ΔG = −19.6 and −27.8 kcal/mol, respectively). Immune simulations predicted robust humoral and cellular responses, including strong antibody production and interferon-γ induction for VC2.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a foundation for the development of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate with broad immunogenic potential against MPXV, which could enhance global preparedness for mpox outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: While these computational findings lay a solid foundation, VC2 requires further experimental validation and preclinical development as a targeted vaccine strategy against MPXV.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to design a broadly immunogenic multi-epitope vaccine against the Monkeypox virus (MPXV) using a conservation-guided immunoinformatics approach. The researchers analyzed 27 complete MPXV genomes from 2001 to 2025 to identify highly conserved viral genes and prioritize surface-exposed proteins for epitope prediction. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on binding affinity, antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and absence of human sequence homology. Three vaccine constructs were designed, and structural modeling, molecular docking, immune response simulation, and codon optimization were performed to evaluate their properties. VC2 was predicted to have the strongest interactions with TLR2 and TLR4–MD-2, achieving the highest binding affinities. Immune simulations suggested robust humoral and cellular responses for VC2. The study estimated 99.27% global coverage for the vaccine constructs and predicted stability, antigenicity, and non-allergenic properties. However, the computational findings require further experimental validation and preclinical development for practical application.

title: Public Knowledge, Attitudes, and Preventive Practices Regarding Mpox in Bangladesh: Insights From a Community-Based Cross-Sectional Survey.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox has recently re-emerged as a significant global health concern, highlighting the importance of public awareness and preventive measures. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding Mpox and its epidemiology, prevention, and control measures among the general population of Bangladesh.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted from June 2024 to September 2024 among 1002 participants across 16 districts. The study focused on the general population of Bangladesh, using a multi-stage random sampling approach following STROBE guidelines.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Both univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to determine associations between sociodemographic factors and KAP outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Out of 1002 respondents, only 37.2% demonstrated good knowledge of Mpox, while 74.0% had positive attitudes, and 80.0% reported satisfactory preventive practices. Higher education was strongly associated with good knowledge (AOR = 11.8; 95% CI: 5.61-25.8), positive attitudes (AOR = 5.68; 95% CI: 2.63-12.5), and satisfactory practices (AOR = 6.49; 95% CI: 2.62-16.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that gaps in awareness and training are associated with suboptimal practices, highlighting potential areas for targeted educational interventions. Attitudes and practices showed the strongest correlation (ρ = 0.793, p < 0.001), indicating a strong association between attitudes and preventive practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Awareness of Mpox as a viral disease was limited (37.3%), and only 22.5% knew about the protective role of smallpox vaccination. Strengthening community-level awareness and preparedness may support public health readiness for potential Mpox outbreaks in Bangladesh.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on self-reported data and associations rather than direct biological or clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated public knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding Mpox in Bangladesh through a community-based cross-sectional survey conducted from June to September 2024. The survey included 1002 participants across 16 districts, using a structured questionnaire and logistic regression analyses. Results showed that only 37.2% of respondents had good knowledge of Mpox, while 74.0% had positive attitudes and 80.0% reported satisfactory preventive practices. Higher education was strongly linked to better KAP outcomes, and attitudes and practices were closely correlated. The authors suggest that gaps in awareness and training may lead to suboptimal practices, emphasizing the need for targeted educational interventions. The study's findings highlight the importance of improving community awareness to enhance public health readiness for potential Mpox outbreaks. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate due to reliance on self-reported data.

title: Geospatial analysis and predictive modelling of mpox transmission hotspots: a case study of Ogun State, Nigeria

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the recurring public health threat of mpox in Nigeria, particularly the need for more precise risk models at the Local Government Area (LGA) level to improve targeted interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated an LGA-resolution geospatial risk layer for Ogun State, Nigeria, using 191 spatially disaggregated pseudo-presence points from 40 laboratory-confirmed and 151 suspected mpox cases, and integrated it into a live surveillance platform.
analysis.methods: The researchers used an ensemble of maximum entropy, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting models over 100 bootstrap replicates to develop and validate the geospatial risk layer.
analysis.main_results: The geospatial risk layer showed good discrimination under random hold-out (AUC 0.77; Boyce index 0.99) but poor performance under spatially blocked cross-validation (AUC 0.57), indicating its suitability for coarse triage rather than detailed ranking.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study's tiered risk layer was integrated into the IDS-Master platform as a proof-of-concept for translating spatial epidemiology into routine public health surveillance, offering a novel approach to mpox risk assessment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The tiered risk layer can inform targeted public health interventions, improve resource allocation, and enhance surveillance efforts in Ogun State, Nigeria, by providing a spatial prioritization tool for mpox risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on pseudo-presence points and the poor performance under spatially blocked cross-validation limit the layer's precision and generalizability, suggesting that further validation is needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed and evaluated an LGA-resolution geospatial risk layer for Ogun State, Nigeria, using 191 pseudo-presence points from mpox cases. The layer showed good discrimination under random hold-out but poor performance under spatially blocked cross-validation, indicating its suitability for coarse triage rather than detailed ranking. The tiered risk layer was integrated into the IDS-Master platform, offering a novel approach to mpox risk assessment and informing targeted public health interventions.

title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance in Wastewater, North Carolina, USA, October 2023–May 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: In September 2023, the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services identified a new case of mpox clade II 5 months after the last previous report, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance to detect possible unrecognized transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To assess possible unrecognized transmission, nonvariola orthopoxvirus testing was implemented at select wastewater sites during October 29, 2023–May 2025, across 16 treatment plants serving approximately 2 million residents.
analysis.methods: During October 29, 2023–May 2025, a total of 801 samples were collected across 16 treatment plants serving ≈2 million residents. We analyzed wastewater detections (n = 47) and clinical cases (n = 45) using a +17-day window.
analysis.main_results: Overall sensitivity of identifying the presence of >1 temporally aligned mpox case within a sewershed was 10.6% (95% CI 6.5%–16.7%); specificity was 95.1% (95% CI 93.2%–96.5%), positive predictive value was 31.9% (95% CI 20.4%–46.2%), and negative predictive value was 83.2% (95% CI 80.3%–85.7%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Restricting detections above the limit of detection reduced sensitivity but increased specificity, indicating a trade-off in detection accuracy based on threshold settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance showed low sensitivity but provided complementary awareness for public health response, supporting the use of this method as an adjunct to clinical monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study found that wastewater surveillance had low sensitivity, which may limit its effectiveness in detecting all cases, but the evidence is moderate in strength due to the clear reporting of statistical measures.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the utility of wastewater surveillance for detecting mpox virus transmission in North Carolina. From October 2023 to May 2025, 801 samples were collected from 16 wastewater treatment plants. The analysis revealed that wastewater testing had low sensitivity but high specificity, with a 10.6% sensitivity and 95.1% specificity in identifying temporally aligned mpox cases. The findings suggest that wastewater surveillance can complement clinical monitoring for public health response, though its limited sensitivity may affect its reliability. The study's evidence is moderate in strength, as it provides statistical measures but does not address broader ecological or transmission dynamics.

title: Mpox (Formerly Known as Monkeypox) in Dermatological Practice: Presentation of a Series of Four Clinical Cases at a Referral Hospital

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to highlight the evolving clinical spectrum of mpox and reinforce dermatology's role in early recognition and diagnosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a retrospective case series of four confirmed mpox cases diagnosed at a tertiary dermatology center in Jalisco, Mexico, between April 2025 and May 2025. All patients were men who have sex with men (MSM), with three living with HIV, reflecting the epidemiologic patterns observed in other regions.
analysis.methods: Diagnosis was confirmed by PCR and supported by compatible histopathology when performed. PCR and biopsy results were consistent with mpox, and the diagnostic process was aided by thorough sexual and travel history-taking.
analysis.main_results: All patients reported recent sexual exposure, with one patient having more than 100 male sexual partners and recent high-risk anal contact. The cases demonstrated clinical heterogeneity, including isolated perianal lesions and mucosal involvement with odynophagia preceding cutaneous findings. Biopsy showed findings consistent with mpox.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the clinical presentations of mpox in dermatologic practice are diverse, ranging from classic disseminated disease to localized anogenital forms. This highlights the need for broad differential diagnosis and the importance of epidemiologic context in early detection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for mpox in patients with vesiculopustular, mucosal, genital, or anogenital lesions, particularly when epidemiologic risk factors are present. They also support the need for continued surveillance to better understand transmission patterns and clinical behavior.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a small number of cases from a single tertiary referral center, which may affect generalizability. However, the confirmed diagnoses and consistent clinical presentations provide moderate evidence for the observed patterns.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a case series of four confirmed mpox cases diagnosed at a tertiary dermatology center in Jalisco, Mexico, in April 2025. The cases highlight the evolving clinical spectrum of mpox, with presentations ranging from classic disseminated disease to localized anogenital forms. All patients were men who have sex with men (MSM), and three were living with HIV, consistent with global epidemiologic trends. Diagnosis was confirmed by PCR and supported by histopathology. The study underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for mpox in patients with vesiculopustular or mucosal lesions, particularly when risk factors such as recent sexual exposure are present. However, the small sample size and single-center design limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate confidence in the observed patterns.

title: HECA-YOLOv11: A High-Accuracy Hybrid Attention Network for Real-Time Monkeypox Skin Lesion Detection with Interpretability

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the urgent public-health need for rapid, accurate diagnostic tools to mitigate the global outbreak risk of mpox, highlighting that existing methods are slow and deep learning models lack both accuracy and interpretability for multi-class skin lesion classification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed and evaluated a deep learning framework (HECA-YOLOv11) designed for real-time screening of mpox and similar skin lesions using a four-class image dataset.
analysis.methods: The proposed architecture integrates a Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11, applying Global Average Pooling and Max Average Pooling to input feature maps, and augments a dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements.
analysis.main_results: On the test set, HECA-YOLOv11 achieved 98.9% accuracy, 99% precision, 99.3% recall, and 99.1% F1-score, outperforming EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, YOLOv11s, SE-YOLOv11, and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all metrics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the integrated attention mechanism and interpretability techniques as effectively addressing key limitations in automated skin lesion detection, marking a major advancement toward reliable clinical decision support for early mpox screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The standardized interface and high performance of HECA-YOLOv11 suggest potential to accelerate public health responses and improve global control of emerging infectious diseases through early detection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report dataset size, geographic or demographic scope, external validation, or prospective clinical evaluation, limiting generalisability and leaving the strength of evidence moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces HECA-YOLOv11, a deep learning framework that integrates a Highly Efficient Channel Attention mechanism into YOLOv11 to improve real-time detection of mpox skin lesions. Using a four-class dataset augmented with spatial and pixel-domain enhancements, the model achieved 98.9% accuracy, 99% precision, 99.3% recall, and 99.1% F1-score on the test set, outperforming multiple baselines by over 5.1% across all metrics. Heatmap analysis via Grad-CAM confirmed lesion-focused attention, and a PyQt5 interface was developed to streamline clinical workflows. The authors argue this represents a major advancement toward reliable clinical decision support for early mpox screening and could accelerate public health responses. However, the abstract-only evidence lacks dataset size, external validation, and prospective clinical evaluation, constraining generalisability and evidence strength.

title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap

analysis.scope_and_question: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications.

analysis.summary_en: This rapid review examines healthcare workers' (HCWs) preparedness for monkeypox (Mpox) pandemic response in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). The review highlights that only 46.8% of HCWs have adequate knowledge about Mpox, despite its high case fatality rate in the region. Barriers to preparedness include reliance on social media for information and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention are associated with higher knowledge levels, but these attitudes do not translate into clinical preparedness, indicating an intention-action gap. The review underscores the need for peer-reviewed information sources and a structured One Health training framework to address these gaps. The findings suggest that targeted training and policy interventions are essential to improve HCW readiness for Mpox outbreaks in SSA.

title: Climate Change, Ecosystem Loss, and Emerging Infectious Diseases in Nigeria

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the relationship between climate change, ecosystem loss, and emerging infectious diseases, with a focus on the Mpox virus. It explores how environmental changes influence the transmission dynamics, host abundance, and disease recognition of the Mpox virus, particularly in the context of Nigeria's diverse ecological zones and healthcare systems.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a critical narrative synthesis of literature on climatic variability, land-use change, biodiversity, transmission ecology, and disease surveillance. It prioritizes Nigerian empirical studies and uses regional or global research to clarify mechanisms, while emphasizing the need for local evidence. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but instead focuses on qualitative synthesis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that Mpox virus transmission is influenced by ecological and climatic factors, but the evidence is limited and heterogeneous. It underscores the importance of pathogen-specific One Health monitoring and the need for prospective ecological–clinical cohorts to better understand the interplay between environmental changes and Mpox outbreaks.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited direct evidence linking ecosystem loss to Mpox outbreaks, and the review notes that findings from related viruses like variola virus or smallpox cannot be directly applied to Mpox. Additionally, the review identifies gaps in longitudinal studies that link ecosystem disturbance, infected hosts, and confirmed human infections.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends out-of-sample validation of ecological warnings, controlled evaluation of water, vector, and household interventions, and the development of prospective ecological–clinical cohorts to improve understanding of Mpox transmission dynamics in relation to environmental changes.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the impact of climate change and ecosystem loss on Mpox virus transmission in Nigeria. It emphasizes the need for pathogen-specific One Health monitoring and highlights the limitations of current evidence, which is often indirect or based on related viruses. The review calls for more rigorous studies to link environmental changes with Mpox outbreaks and suggests actionable research priorities, including prospective ecological–clinical cohorts and controlled interventions. While the evidence is heterogeneous and limited, the review underscores the importance of demonstrating infectious-disease benefits through climate adaptation and ecosystem protection.

title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction.
analysis.methods: The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, "sample-to-eluate" workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes.
analysis.main_results: In DNA-spiked aqueous samples (5-20 ng mL-1), the device demonstrated recoveries of 84.6%, against 90.7% on the bench. The device's clinical utility was piloted using patient samples positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV), monkeypox virus (MPXV) or chikungunya (CHIKV). The device achieved successful qPCR amplification for all targets, with viral DNA Cq values within as little as 0.3 cycles of the standard protocol.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The device's performance in DNA extraction and qPCR amplification for various targets suggests its potential for POC diagnostics, particularly in resource-limited settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This instrument-free, manual circulating nucleic acid extraction tool could help bridge the gap between lateral flow based nucleic acid amplification technologies and real-world decentralised diagnostics, offering a scalable solution for infectious disease management in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Recovery from human pooled plasma samples were found to be on average 18, 62, and 552% higher than that obtained with the control bench extraction on initial sample volumes of 100, 75 and 50 μL, respectively. The device's performance was benchmarked against a commercial magnetic bead-based manual benchtop and an automated robotic workflow.

analysis.summary_en: The study introduces a finger-actuated microfluidic device for nucleic acid extraction, demonstrating its effectiveness in DNA extraction and qPCR amplification for various targets, including monkeypox virus (MPXV), in resource-limited settings.

title: Disciform Keratitis That Improves With Poly(Adenosine Diphosphate-Ribose) Polymerase Inhibitor Treatment for Ovarian Cancer but Recurs Upon Discontinuation of Treatment

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the relationship between immune status and the clinical course of disciform keratitis, particularly in the context of systemic immunosuppression caused by cancer treatments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a single patient with a history of ovarian cancer who developed disciform keratitis following discontinuation of PARP inhibitor therapy, highlighting the clinical course and immune status changes in this individual.
analysis.methods: Disciform keratitis was diagnosed via slit-lamp examination, and VZV DNA was detected using PCR analysis of aqueous humor. The patient was treated with oral valacyclovir and topical betamethasone, with clinical improvement observed.
analysis.main_results: Disciform keratitis resolved during PARP inhibitor treatment, which induced systemic immunosuppression, but recurred one year after discontinuation. PCR analysis confirmed the presence of VZV DNA in the aqueous humor.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that immune suppression from PARP inhibitors may prevent reactivation of VZV, leading to resolution of disciform keratitis, while immune recovery upon treatment discontinuation may reactivate the virus, causing recurrence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the importance of monitoring immune status in cancer patients to manage ocular complications like disciform keratitis, particularly those associated with viral reactivation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single case, and the association observed does not establish causality. The evidence is considered moderate due to the lack of comparative data and immunological verification.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a patient with ovarian cancer who developed disciform keratitis following discontinuation of PARP inhibitor treatment. The condition resolved during treatment with the PARP inhibitor, which induced systemic immunosuppression, but recurred one year after treatment cessation. PCR analysis of aqueous humor confirmed the presence of varicella-zoster virus (VZV) DNA, suggesting a link between immune status and the clinical course of disciform keratitis. The findings imply that immune suppression may prevent viral reactivation, while immune recovery could lead to recurrence. However, the study is limited to a single case and does not establish causality, resulting in moderate evidence strength. The report underscores the need to monitor immune status in cancer patients to manage ocular complications associated with viral reactivation.

analysis.main_results: Se abordaron las principales ITS relevantes en este contexto –gonorrea, clamidiasis, tricomoniasis, sífilis, VIH/SIDA, hepatitis A, B y C, herpes simple, virus del papiloma humano y Mpox–, detallando indicaciones de toma de muestras, períodos ventana, esquemas terapéuticos, profilaxis post exposición, vacunación y seguimiento serológico.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Estas recomendaciones buscan estandarizar el abordaje infectológico de niños, niñas y adolescentes víctimas de violencia sexual en Chile, optimizando la pesquisa precoz, el tratamiento oportuno y las estrategias preventivas, en concordancia con la normativa nacional vigente.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Las recomendaciones pueden informar la práctica clínica en el manejo de ITS en niños, niñas y adolescentes víctimas de violencia sexual, mejorando la detección temprana, el tratamiento adecuado y la implementación de estrategias preventivas en el contexto chileno.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: El documento se basa en una revisión crítica de literatura y consenso de expertos, lo cual puede limitar la generalización de los hallazgos. La evidencia es moderada, ya que no se reportan estudios originales o datos estadísticos específicos.

The methods involved analyzing the most relevant STIs, including mpox, and detailing sampling protocols, window periods, therapeutic schemes, post-exposure prophylaxis, vaccination, and serological follow-up. The authors interpret these findings as a means to standardize the infectious approach in this population, aligning with national regulations. The scientific and public health significance lies in the potential to improve early detection, timely treatment, and preventive strategies in Chile. However, the evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on literature review and expert consensus rather than original studies or statistical data.
